questions.reason: The captured text states inference logs are 'automatically collected chat completions generated via API or Playground (unless Zero Data Retention is enabled)', directly supporting the correct option. No other option is defensible from the page.
The EmbeddingRequest schema in the captured text marks `required: [model, input]`, which matches 'the model and the input text'. The other options each omit at least one required field.

The captured page lists both triggers verbatim: 'At the start of the month, if your balance is negative' and 'When the configured billing threshold is reached'. The correct option combines them faithfully; the distractors describe triggers the page does not mention.

The captured text describes streaming as 'data-only server-sent events' terminated by 'data: [DONE]', exactly matching the correct option. WebSocket, multipart, and single-array delivery are not described.

The captured text says 'lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic', directly supporting the correct option. The distractors over-claim (guaranteed identical output, auto-disable of top_p) or invert the direction.

The captured text states 'Local SSD disks are ephemeral, meaning temporary: their data is erased when the VM is stopped or deleted', which directly supports the correct option. None of the other options match the page.

The captured text states 'One shared filesystem can be attached to multiple VMs at once', directly supporting the correct option. Network SSD disks are limited to one VM at a time, and the other options are not concurrent-share mechanisms.
The captured text states 'The size of each namespace is 93 GiB, so the disk size must be a multiple of 93 GiB.' Since 100 is not a multiple of 93, the rejection is explained.

The captured text states 'Sharing a filesystem across projects is not supported, even if the projects are in the same region', directly supporting the correct option. Tenant scope, virtiofs, and encryption are not the binding constraint.

The captured text defines `compute.instance-power-operator` as 'perform power operations on virtual machines without broader Compute permissions', exactly matching the scenario. The other roles are either too broad or for different tasks.

The captured text defines `storage.uploader` as 'view buckets, upload objects but not list or download them', which exactly matches the write-only-drop requirement. The other roles either grant reading, listing, or broader access.

The captured text states 'For an existing project, you can only edit the name. You cannot move a project to another region or tenant.' Only option d is consistent with this; all others claim a change the page forbids.

The captured text warns under the CLI tab: 'If you try to create a project in a private region, you receive an error.' The question specifies CLI use, so the warning applies directly. The other explanations are not what the page says.

The captured text states 'you can create, activate, deactivate and delete federations, change their settings, and upload or delete attached certificates.' Uploading the new cert and deleting the old one on the existing federation is what the page describes.

The captured text's prerequisites require being in a group 'that has the `admin` role within your tenant or project', so an editor without admin cannot manage federations. The correct option captures this restriction.

The captured text lists as a prerequisite that you can get 'the SAML application metadata (login URL, identifier, certificate)' from the IdP portal, directly supporting the correct option. The distractors describe things never handed over or irrelevant to federation setup.

The captured text states 'The VM usage data becomes available 5–10 minutes after the VM is created.' Two minutes is within that window, so waiting is the appropriate response. Reinstalling or escalating would be premature.
The captured text states 'By default, the data is refreshed every 15 seconds. You can configure this interval next to the time filters.', directly supporting the correct option.

The captured text states VMs 'count towards the quotas throughout the VM's lifecycle, from its creation to deletion, regardless of whether it is running or stopped.' Stopping does not release quota; only deletion does.

The captured text states 'These quotas apply to Compute VMs and also to Managed Service for Soperator and Managed Service for Kubernetes® nodes, which are based on Compute VMs.' K8s nodes count against the same Compute quotas.
The captured text states 'Compute has different quotas for GPU and non-GPU virtual machines.' The correct option is the necessary correction to the single-quota assumption.

The captured text describes rerank as reordering documents 'based on their relevance to a query', and the RerankResult schema includes `index`, `document`, and `relevance_score` as required fields. The correct option names the result fields accurately.
